statement.summary: Theorem 6.1 is the core frozen Prop `ShiftSym.lowerBoundStatement n dd σ` (Statement.lean, frozen in Phase E): under 2 ≤ n, 1 ≤ dd, 2 ≤ σ, `lowerEnvelope n dd σ ≤ |S|` (in ℤ) and `lowerEnvelope n dd σ = |S| ↔ n.Prime`. It is not restated in Phase H; S06 adds the bridge from the paper's product-formula F_d to `lowerEnvelope`, and S10/S06 contain restatements of its halves (`primeEqualityStatement`, `strictCompositeStatement`, `primesMeetEnvelopeStatement`).
deltas: |S_{n^d}| is `Nat.card` of the subtype of shift-symmetric configurations, cast to ℤ; F_d and the comparison live in ℤ.

Gaussian binomials use the q-Pascal recurrence `gaussBinom`, evaluated at q = n; agreement with the paper's product formula at every integer q ≥ 2 is certified separately (`P06.gaussProdEq_proved`, `P06.envelopeIntegral_proved`).
n^{d−r} uses ℕ-subtraction `dd - r`, exact on 1 ≤ r ≤ d.
σ ≥ 2 is kept (not relaxed to σ ≥ 1): the equality clause is false at σ = 1.

maps.label: Theorem 6.1: F_d ≤ |S|, equality iff n prime

tex.text: with equality if and only if $n$ is prime

maps.note: The frozen Prop is the conjunction of the inequality and the equality-iff-prime clause, under the three hypotheses as antecedents. It was frozen in Statement.lean before the proof (Phase E).

maps.label: n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: Stated in the theorem itself (matching the standing hypotheses of Definition 2.1). The dimension variable is called `dd` in Lean.

maps.label: σ ≥ 2 (not σ ≥ 1)
maps.note: Not a counting statement in the sense of Definition 2.1: the equality clause fails at σ = 1 (e.g. d = 1: F_1 = 1 = |S_n| for every n), so σ ≥ 2 is required and kept.

maps.label: standing setting of Definition 2.1

tex.text:
Fix integers $n\ge2$, $d\ge1$ and a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with
$\sigma=|\Sigma|\ge2$

maps.note: The theorem's hypotheses coincide with the standing ones; the alphabet is fixed as `Fin σ` (only |Σ| enters).

maps.label: |S_{n^d}| ≥ F_d(n,σ)

lean.text:
lowerEnvelope n dd σ
        ≤ (Nat.card {s : Config n dd (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s} : ℤ)

maps.note: Written as F_d ≤ |S| in ℤ: the envelope is an alternating sum, so the comparison is made in ℤ with the count cast from ℕ.

maps.label: |S_{n^d}|

lean.text: (Nat.card {s : Config n dd (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s} : ℤ)

maps.note: |S_{n^d}| is `Nat.card` of the subtype of shift-symmetric configurations over the alphabet `Fin σ`, cast to ℤ.

maps.label: S_{n^d} = ⋃_{v≠0} S_{n^d}(v)

lean.text: ∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: s ∈ S_{n^d} iff some nonzero translation fixes s; `IsShiftSymmetric` says exactly that (∃ v ≠ 0, shift v s = s).

maps.label: configurations s : 𝒜 → Σ on 𝒜 = (ℤ/nℤ)^d
maps.note: 𝒜 = `Lat n d = Fin d → ZMod n`; configurations are functions `Lat n d → Fin σ`.

maps.label: translation (τ_v s)(u) = s(u+v)
maps.note: Same convention (u + v, not u − v).

maps.label: F_d(n,σ)
maps.note: F_d(n,σ) is the project definition `lowerEnvelope n dd σ` (an integer).

maps.label: F_d := Σ_{r=1}^d (−1)^{r+1} n^{C(r,2)} [d r]_n σ^{n^{d−r}}

lean.text:
∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 dd,
    (-1 : ℤ) ^ (r + 1) * (rdCoeff n r dd : ℤ) * (σ : ℤ) ^ (n ^ (dd - r))

maps.note: Term-by-term the same sum, in ℤ; the coefficient n^{C(r,2)}[d r]_n is packaged as `rdCoeff n r dd`.

maps.label: r = 1,…,d
maps.note: Index set [1, d].

maps.label: (−1)^{r+1}
maps.note: Sign in ℤ.

maps.label: n^{C(r,2)} [d r]_n = r_d(n, r)
maps.note: `rdCoeff q v d = q^{C(v,2)} · gaussBinom q d v`, evaluated at the (possibly composite) q = n; a natural number cast to ℤ.

maps.label: n^{C(r,2)}
maps.note: C(r,2) is `Nat.choose r 2`; q := n, v := r.

maps.label: [d r]_n (Gaussian binomial at q = n)
maps.note: Lean's Gaussian binomial is defined by the q-Pascal recurrence, the paper's by the product formula; see the next map for the bridge.

maps.label: product formula = q-Pascal recurrence (bridge)

tex.text:
we will evaluate Gaussian binomials at the (possibly
composite) integer argument $q=n$

lean.text: gaussProd q d r = (gaussBinom q d r : ℚ)
paperEnvelope n d σ = (lowerEnvelope n d σ : ℚ)

maps.note: Not part of the frozen statement, but certified in Phase H (`gaussProdEq_proved`, `envelopeIntegral_proved`): at every integer q ≥ 2 the two definitions agree, and the paper's F_d written with the product formula (`paperEnvelope`, in ℚ) equals `lowerEnvelope`.

maps.label: σ^{n^{d−r}}
maps.note: Integer power in ℤ.

maps.label: n^{d−r} (ℕ-subtraction)
maps.note: `dd - r` is truncated ℕ-subtraction; exact on the summation range r ≤ d.

maps.label: equality iff n prime

tex.text: with equality if and only if $n$ is prime

lean.text:
lowerEnvelope n dd σ
          = (Nat.card {s : Config n dd (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s} : ℤ)
        ↔ n.Prime

maps.note: Both directions: F_d = |S| ⇔ n prime (under the same hypotheses).

maps.label: n is prime
maps.note: mathlib's `Nat.Prime`.
